title: How long can you last?
principle: Businesses die when cash runs out, not when profit does.

screens.text: Let me start with a story. In December 2018, Jet Airways had 119 planes flying across India. Four months later, none of them could fly. Before I tell you why, have a guess.

screens.prompt: What do you think stopped such a big airline from flying?
screens.why: It ran out of cash. Most people expect a big reason, but the problem was simple: Jet could not pay for fuel, and its pilots had not been paid for months.

screens.title: Cash going down
screens.text: So how did such a big airline run out of cash? Each month, more money went out than came in. Jet had to pay for fuel, salaries and plane rent. Ticket money was not enough, so the cash in its bank kept going down.

screens.title: Your runway
screens.text: Think of the cash in a bank as petrol in a tank, and a monthly loss as a leak in that tank. The one number I want you to know is how many months are left before the tank runs dry. That number is your runway.

screens.prompt: Let's try one. A business has ₹30 lakh in the bank and loses ₹5 lakh every month. How long is its runway?
screens.why: Exactly. ₹30 lakh divided by ₹5 lakh is 6 months. That is the runway sum: cash in the bank divided by cash lost each month. If nothing changes, this owner has 6 months to fix the business or get more money.

wrong.a: Close. Let me show you the sum: ₹30 lakh divided by ₹5 lakh is 6, so if nothing changes, the cash lasts 6 months.
wrong.c: Not quite. ₹30 lakh is the cash you have, not the number of months. Divide it by the ₹5 lakh lost each month, and you get 6 months.

screens.prompt: Jet's cash was running low, so it asked its banks for ₹400 crore. Why might a bank still say no?

options.label: The losses hadn't stopped, so the loan would also run out
₹400 crore was too small to matter

screens.why: Exactly. ₹400 crore could give Jet more time, but it would not stop the losses. If Jet kept losing cash, this new money would also run out. The banks said no, and on 17 April 2019 Jet flew its last flight.

wrong.a: Banks do lend to airlines. But think like the bank. If I lend you money and your business keeps losing cash, how will you pay me back?
wrong.c: ₹400 crore could pay for a lot of fuel and wages. But if Jet kept losing cash, the new money would only help for some time.

screens.title: Now look at your business
screens.text: Jet had planes and crores of rupees, but the same problem can close a small shop too. So let us use a smaller example. Imagine you have opened a small gym. Let us see how long your cash will last.

screens.prompt: Your gym has ₹3 lakh in the bank. ₹1.5 lakh goes out each month, and members pay you ₹1 lakh. What's your runway?
screens.why: Well done. ₹1.5 lakh goes out, but ₹1 lakh comes back in, so your cash only shrinks by ₹50,000 a month. That means ₹3 lakh gives you 6 months of runway.

wrong.a: I see what you did: ₹3 lakh divided by ₹1.5 lakh. But your members still pay you ₹1 lakh, so your real monthly loss is only ₹50,000, and your runway is 6 months.
wrong.b: You're close, but find the gap first. ₹1.5 lakh out minus ₹1 lakh in leaves a loss of ₹50,000 a month, and ₹3 lakh divided by ₹50,000 gives you 6 months.

screens.prompt: Your gym has ₹3 lakh and loses ₹50,000 a month. Which choice gives you the most runway?

options.label: Put ₹50,000 more into the bank, once
Sign 10 new members at ₹1,000 a month

screens.why: Exactly. Your monthly loss falls from ₹50,000 to ₹25,000, so the same ₹3 lakh now lasts 12 months. You did not add more cash. You reduced the monthly loss, so the cash you already have lasts longer.

wrong.b: That helps. ₹3.5 lakh divided by ₹50,000 gives you 7 months. But you still lose ₹50,000 every month. Cutting ₹25,000 of costs lowers the loss every month and gives you 12 months.
wrong.c: That helps too. Ten members bring in ₹10,000 more, so your loss falls to ₹40,000. That gives you about 7½ months. Cutting ₹25,000 of costs lowers the loss more and gives you 12 months.

screens.prompt: Your trainers' ₹20,000 is due on Saturday. I'll show you six things. For each one, tell me: can you spend it today?

items.text: A company says it will buy 20 memberships next month
₹30,000 a member must pay you in 60 days
A GST refund you expect soon

screens.why: Exactly. The ₹8,000 by UPI and the ₹12,000 in your account make the ₹20,000 you need. The other things may bring money later, but you cannot spend that money this Saturday. Runway counts only cash you can use now.

screens.setup: A local company offers you a big deal. It wants memberships for 40 staff, worth ₹40,000 a month. But you must first buy ₹1.5 lakh of new machines. The company usually pays only after three months.
screens.question: You have 6 months of runway. What can you do to take this deal without putting the gym at risk?

options.label: Say yes and buy the machines today
options.outcome: Your bank falls from ₹3 lakh to ₹1.5 lakh at once. You still lose ₹50,000 each month. After three months, when the company's first payment is due, that ₹1.5 lakh is gone.
options.why: The deal brings money later, but you must pay much earlier. Before saying yes to a big order, check how much cash will be left before the customer pays.
options.better: Ask for the first three months in advance, or rent the machines.

options.label: Say yes, if they pay three months up front
options.outcome: They pay ₹1.2 lakh first. That is three months of fees. So you use only ₹30,000 of your own cash for the machines. After that, ₹40,000 comes in each month, and your monthly loss falls from ₹50,000 to ₹10,000.
options.why: Exactly. You changed when the customer pays. The deal is still worth the same amount. But now the advance pays for most of the machines instead of using your ₹3 lakh.

options.label: Say no. It's too risky
options.outcome: You keep your ₹3 lakh, but the ₹50,000 monthly loss carries on, your runway stays at 6 months, and the company takes the deal to another gym.
options.why: That is safer than spending without checking. But there was a better choice: ask the company to pay earlier before you give up the deal.
options.better: Ask for an advance before you say no.

screens.text: A business doesn't shut when its profit runs out. It shuts when its ___ runs out, and the months it has left are its ___.
screens.why: Exactly. In April 2019, Jet still had planes and loyal customers. But those things could not pay for fuel and wages that day. When usable cash becomes zero, a business can stop even if it still owns valuable things. That is why I want you to watch your runway.

summary: Your runway is how many months your cash lasts: cash in the bank ÷ monthly loss.
Count only the gap between money out and money in.
Fixing the leak beats topping up the tank, and every big deal should be checked against your runway.

cards.front: You make ₹20,000 profit a month, but buyers pay in 90 days. What should you watch most?
options: Cash in the bank each week
cards.back: Cash. Profit that arrives in 90 days can't pay this week's bills.

cards.front: ₹2,40,000 in the bank. You lose ₹40,000 a month. How long can you last?
A big new order pays in 90 days. What makes it safe?
cards.back: Bring the cash closer. Growth on long credit empties the bank.
